articles.title: Kashmir on a Plate: What the Swiss President Ate at Rashtrapati Bhavan
articles.excerpt: President Droupadi Murmu's October 6 banquet for Guy Parmelin served a Kashmiri-Ladakhi spread — Nadur Kebab, Dum Oluv, Shufta and more — during his three-day India visit.
articles.image_caption: Swiss President Guy Parmelin poses with President Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan. The October 6 state banquet served a Kashmiri-Ladakhi menu including Nadur Kebab, Dum Oluv, and Shufta.
articles.nri_angle: The Kashmiri-Ladakhi banquet showcased regional Indian cuisine as soft power, giving the diaspora a proud, specific culinary identity to share abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Rented Cows to ₹2.4 Crore: Jaipur Couple's Gir Dairy Dream
articles.excerpt: Vibhor and Ishita Jain started Kinaya Organic Farms in 2018 with no farming experience. Today it runs 100 Gir cows and sells A2 milk and bilona ghee.
articles.image_caption: Gir cows, the indigenous breed at the heart of Kinaya Organic Farms near Jaipur. The Jain family's herd of 100 Gir cows produces 250-300 litres of A2 milk daily.
articles.nri_angle: The Jaipur couple's desi-cow dairy model shows NRI investors and returning professionals a working template for premium, sustainable agribusiness in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: American's Claim That Aloo Bhujia 'Cured' His Asthma Amuses the Internet
articles.excerpt: A Massachusetts man's viral video crediting simple Indian food — illustrated with a packet of aloo bhujia — for curing his asthma and allergies drew a wave of jokes from Indian netizens, and a reminder that anecdotes aren't medical evidence.
articles.nri_angle: A viral moment celebrating Indian food's global appeal — diaspora audiences joined Indians back home in the joke, turning a health claim into a shared food-culture laugh.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: TresInd Studio Holds Onto Three Michelin Stars, Keeping Indian Dining at Dubai's Summit
articles.excerpt: The Palm Jumeirah restaurant retained its three stars in the fifth Michelin Guide Dubai, cementing its standing as the highest-rated Indian restaurant in the world.
articles.image_caption: Chefs and restaurateurs pose on stage at the Michelin Guide Dubai awards ceremony. Trèsind Studio retained its Three Michelin Stars in the guide's fifth edition, announced this week.
articles.nri_angle: Trèsind Studio's three-star retention gives Dubai's Indian community a pride-of-place dining room and NRIs a bucket-list booking for Gulf visits.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Turmeric, Cumin and Coriander: The Ancient Trio Behind India's Lentils and Curries
articles.excerpt: The centuries-old foundation of Indian cooking is three everyday spices — and the Ayurvedic logic of warming and cooling that makes them work together.
articles.image_caption: Turmeric, cumin and coriander — the ancient trio at the heart of India's lentils and curries.
articles.nri_angle: A practical diaspora-kitchen win: turmeric, cumin, and coriander are cheap and available in any Indian grocery store abroad, and the trio covers a week of meals — a centuries-old shortcut that beats pre-mixed masalas for control.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Maharashtra's 'Food Safety Rock Star' Tukaram Mundhe Lands on New York Times Front Page
articles.excerpt: The Maharashtra FDA commissioner's 12,000-inspection crackdown — from a 100-year-old Mumbai café to Blinkit dark stores — earned him a front-page NYT profile: "In India, a Food Inspector Is a Rock Star."
articles.image_caption: Maharashtra FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe poses beside the October 4 New York Times front page featuring his food safety crackdown. The paper called him a rock star whom diners revere and owners fear.
articles.nri_angle: Mumbai's food scene is familiar ground for the diaspora, and the quick-commerce dark-store model Mundhe is raiding is the same instant-delivery playbook spreading to Indian diaspora markets abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Gold Prices Today: 24K Gold Slips ₹160 to ₹1.49 Lakh as Festive Season Buying Begins
articles.excerpt: 24K gold eased to around ₹1.49 lakh per 10 grams on Tuesday, October 6, after Monday's sharper ₹1,100 drop; silver held near ₹2.25 lakh per kg across major cities.
articles.image_caption: A stock image of gold bars and coins beside a rising price chart labeled Gold Price Today. Retail gold prices eased on October 6, with 24K gold near ₹1.49 lakh per 10 grams in most Indian cities.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs visiting India for the festive and wedding season face record-high gold prices, making 22K jewellery buys significantly costlier; verifying BIS hallmarking, comparing making charges, and factoring in 3% GST matters more than ever at these levels.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Paneer Costs Seven Times More Per Gram of Protein Than Masoor Dal
articles.excerpt: With paneer and pulse prices climbing, ThePrint argues India must grow far more protein — while households can stretch their protein rupee by leaning on cheaper dals.
articles.image_caption: Milk is poured from a steel vessel into a large container at a dairy facility. ThePrint's analysis found paneer costs nearly seven times more per gram of protein than masoor dal, while processors are expanding paneer capacity on rising demand.
articles.nri_angle: For the diaspora's largely vegetarian households, the same protein math holds at the grocery aisle: dal and pulses stretch the protein budget farthest, and until India grows enough of them, paneer and pulse prices are likely to keep climbing.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Diwali Gifting Gets Pricier: Pistachio, Almond Prices Surge Ahead of Festival
articles.excerpt: Pistachio prices are up 30–40% and almonds 10–20% as the US-Iran conflict disrupts Iranian supplies, freight rates climb, and a weak rupee inflates import costs — with traders expecting festive sales to fall 10–15%.
articles.image_caption: Pistachios at a dry-fruit market. Pistachio prices in India have risen 30–40 percent year-on-year ahead of Diwali on supply disruptions and higher freight costs.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs sending Diwali hampers to India face the same 15–30% inflation, though almonds bought at the Californian origin may be relatively cheaper than Indian retail.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mom's Biryani Brings Homestyle Dum Biryani to Sunnyvale's Crowded Indian Food Lane
articles.excerpt: The Fremont Avenue restaurant calls itself Sunnyvale's top pick for authentic Indian food — a claim born from its own press release, but diners give it a solid 4.6 out of 5.
articles.image_caption: The Mom's Biryani storefront at 103 East Fremont Avenue in Sunnyvale. The homestyle restaurant holds a 4.6-out-of-5 rating across nearly 400 reviews.
articles.nri_angle: For Bay Area Indians, homestyle spots like Mom's Biryani are everyday infrastructure — the taste of home for tech workers and the go-to for family dinners and celebrations.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Still LA's Best Biryani: The Little Bangladesh Strip-Mall Spot Worth The Drive
articles.excerpt: Eater LA's Rebecca Roland reaffirms the verdict: the city's best biryani is still at Biriyani Kebob House in Little Bangladesh, where a former aeronautical engineer's kitchen turns out Hyderabadi lamb biryani that tastes like home.
articles.image_caption: A plate of biryani served with raita and chutney. (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: For LA's Indian and South Asian community, this Little Bangladesh institution is a fixed point of the diaspora food map — and proof the neighbourhood kitchens still set the standard.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Neemsi: Bengaluru's Vegetarian Restaurant Sourcing Spices Straight From the Farm
articles.excerpt: Two and a half years after opening, the pure-vegetarian restaurant runs two south Bengaluru outlets and buys whole spices directly from farmers in the regions known for them. It says the two outlets have gathered more than 20,000 Google reviews.
articles.image_caption: A promotional image shows a table set with vegetarian dishes, marigold garlands and lit diyas, announcing Neemsi’s Festive Edit menu running 11 September to 15 November. The Bengaluru restaurant’s seasonal menu is timed for Navratri, Durga Puja, Dussehra and Diwali.
articles.nri_angle: A pure-vegetarian, Jain-on-request restaurant with farm-direct sourcing gives visiting diaspora families — grandparents ordering Jain, grandchildren ordering Italian at the same table — a reliable Bengaluru option, and its Festive Edit targets people who cannot travel home for Diwali.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: '$600 for This Breakfast?': Viral Post Revives India-vs-US Hotel Breakfast Debate
articles.excerpt: A viral X post comparing a $600-a-night JW Marriott breakfast in the US with India's lavish spreads has reignited the long-running hospitality debate.
articles.image_caption: A hotel breakfast buffet. A viral post this weekend contrasted a modest 00-a-night US hotel breakfast with far more generous spreads in India.
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs who travel between India and the US, the breakfast gap is a lived twice-a-year experience — and the viral post gives it a $600 price tag.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Three Friends Bet on Kulhad Chai. Now Their Brand Crosses Rs 100 Crore
articles.excerpt: Indore's Chai Sutta Bar grew from a ₹3 lakh first shop to 600+ outlets and ₹100 crore-plus turnover — bootstrapped, franchise-led, and built on ₹10 kulhad chai.
articles.image_caption: Glasses of kulhad chai with the Chai Sutta Bar logo, in an image illustrating the brand's franchise offering. The Indore-based chain has grown to more than 600 outlets across 370 cities and reports turnover of over ₹100 crore.
articles.nri_angle: Chai Sutta Bar's Dubai and Oman outlets are already known to Gulf Indians; its franchise-led, capital-light playbook is a template for Indian-food brands expanding across the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Four Friends Turned a Thailand Street Snack Into a Rs 50 Crore Brand
articles.excerpt: The Croffle Guys landed ₹2.5 crore from Kunal Bahl and Mohit Yadav on Shark Tank India — a ₹50 crore valuation built on croissant-dough waffles and zero ad spend.
articles.image_caption: A croffle — croissant dough pressed in a waffle iron — the Thailand street snack that inspired The Croffle Guys, valued at Rs 50 crore after Shark Tank India
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora entrepreneurs, The Croffle Guys is a case study in the single-product QSR playbook: import a format, localize the palate, grow on organic social content — and let the sharks come to you.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Guwahati Mom, 62, Turned Her Love for Sweets Into a Rs 2.5 Lakh-a-Month Business
articles.excerpt: Sunita Agarwal started Kitchen & Gupshup from her home kitchen in 2022 with four items; today it serves nearly 3,000 customers — and she is helping other women earn from home too.
articles.image_caption: An older woman in a sari prepares sweets by hand in a commercial kitchen, with trays of savouries and her team around her. Sunita Agarwal started Kitchen & Gupshup from her Guwahati home kitchen in 2022; the business now serves nearly 3,000 customers.
articles.nri_angle: For the diaspora, Sunita's story captures how the flavours of home — and the women who carry them — are becoming serious businesses back in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Chennai's Poppadum Turns Jain Food Into Playful Street-Food Adventure
articles.excerpt: The Kilpauk vegetarian diner's new Jain menu runs from Indori bhutte ka kees and pav bhaji quesadillas to a Military Hotel-style potlam biriyani — all without onion, garlic or root vegetables.
articles.image_caption: Crisp papadums — the namesake snack at Poppadum, the Chennai vegetarian diner that has launched a dedicated Jain menu
articles.nri_angle: For the Jain diaspora and NRIs visiting Chennai, the menu shows India's dining scene is professionalising around dietary observance — eating out while keeping Jain rules no longer has to mean compromise.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: US FDA Puts Hyderabad Firm's Fish Masala on Salmonella Import Alert List
articles.excerpt: Fish Masala from Tejas Food Industries LLP can now be detained at the US border without physical examination under Import Alert 99-19; the listing names no specific batch or lab result.
articles.image_caption: A spice product illustration for the FDA import-alert story. The FDA placed Fish Masala made by Hyderabad-based Tejas Food Industries LLP on its Salmonella import-alert Red List, allowing detention of shipments at the US border without physical examination.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian-American shoppers, the alert targets one product from one Hyderabad firm at the US border — not the spice aisle at large — so checking the brand and product name on existing pantry stock is the practical takeaway.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nuh Raids Seize 7,600 kg of Suspected Synthetic Paneer Headed for Delhi-NCR
articles.excerpt: Overnight raids on four unlicensed units in Haryana's Nuh district recovered tonnes of suspected analogue paneer and the chemicals used to make it, in a crackdown aimed at the Delhi-NCR wholesale food chain.
articles.image_caption: A block of paneer with cut cubes on a wooden board. The image accompanies coverage of the September 10-11 raids in Nuh, Haryana, where officials seized nearly 7,600 kg of suspected synthetic paneer.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora readers visiting Delhi-NCR should know cheap bulk paneer in catering and informal markets may be adulterated; genuine paneer lists only milk and acidulants, and the risk is concentrated in unregulated wholesale channels, not branded products at home or abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Inside Elder, Sujan Sarkar's British-Indian Chophouse Reinventing New York Dining
articles.excerpt: The Michelin-starred chef behind Indienne has opened Elder, an à-la-carte British-Indian chophouse at Hudson Yards' Henry Hall — and it may be the clearest sign yet of Indian cuisine's new confidence in America.
articles.image_caption: Chef Sujan Sarkar stands in the open kitchen of Indienne at Henry Hall in New York. He has opened Elder, a British-Indian chophouse, downstairs in the same building.
articles.nri_angle: Elder turns Indian cooking into the house cuisine of a New York dining destination, reflecting the Indian-American dining scene's move from curry-house familiarity to confident, mixed-table ambition.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: FDA Suspends Mumbai Eatery's Licence After Diner Allegedly Finds Rat in Dosa
articles.excerpt: Radhakrishna Hotel in Borivali West lost its food licence after a customer said he found a dead rat in his Mysore masala dosa — the latest flashpoint in FDA chief Tukaram Mundhe's festive-season crackdown.
articles.image_caption: A masala dosa served with chutney and sambar. The FDA suspended a Mumbai eatery's licence after a diner allegedly found a rat in a dosa.
articles.nri_angle: Mumbai's restaurant scene is a pilgrimage stop for visiting NRIs; the crackdown is a reminder that even beloved legacy eateries can fail basic hygiene checks, so diners should trust FSSAI compliance over reputation.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Clermont's Guru Indian Restaurant Marks 12 Years of Northern Indian Classics
articles.excerpt: Master Chef Uday Kadam's family-run Clermont eatery celebrates a dozen years of tandoor-fired favorites — and expands next door with The Venue, a new event space and Sunday brunch.
articles.nri_angle: Master Chef Uday Kadam's journey from a village near Mumbai to Disney to Central Florida — and his restaurant's role as a community gathering place — shows how Indian restaurateurs have become cultural anchors in American suburbs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Recheado Masala: The Fiery Goan Red Paste Every Seafood Lover Should Know
articles.excerpt: Born of Goa's Portuguese heritage, this tangy red masala of chillies, spices and vinegar is the soul of the coast's stuffed-fish fries — and it keeps for days in the fridge.
articles.image_caption: A bowl of recheado masala, the red spice paste of dried red chillies, spices, garlic, tamarind and vinegar. In Goa the paste is traditionally stuffed into mackerel and pomfret before shallow-frying.
articles.nri_angle: Recheado masala is a staple of Goan Catholic kitchens worldwide, and the vinegar-based paste travels well — a make-ahead taste of home for diaspora cooks.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: This 70-Year-Old Hyderabad Shop Bottles Biryani Into a Pickle
articles.excerpt: Qadeem Achar Ghar in Murgi Chowk spent two months perfecting a 20-ingredient, fully vegetarian biryani-flavoured achaar — built for expats missing home.
articles.image_caption: Avakaya, the spicy Andhra mango pickle — the 70-year-old Hyderabad shop sells a biryani-flavoured take on it.
articles.nri_angle: The biryani pickle was created specifically for expats missing the taste of home, and the shop ships vacuum-sealed packs with online ordering.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Chole Kulcha to Rogan Josh: Australian Couple's One-Day Amritsar Food Run Wins the Internet
articles.excerpt: The couple hit Pehelwan Kulcha, Beera Samosa Wala, Gian Di Lassi and Surinder Meat Shop in a single day — and say it's only day one of their journey.
articles.image_caption: Chole kulcha, a highlight of the Australian couple's one-day Amritsar food run.
articles.nri_angle: For Punjabi NRIs, the Amritsar food trail is a map of homesickness — the couple's stops are the landmarks diaspora families describe when they talk about going back.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Beyond the Espresso: How India's Cafés Are Winning Customer Loyalty
articles.excerpt: Food now adds 55% more revenue per customer than beverages alone, and India's cafés — from work cafés to creative studios to craft brands like Subko — are building loyalty through experience, not just espresso.
articles.image_caption: India's café chains are winning customer loyalty with localised menus and community spaces.
articles.nri_angle: The café boom mirrors third-wave coffee culture in the US and UK with a distinctly Indian accent — modern cafés are now a fixture of NRI homecoming itineraries, and the experience-led loyalty playbook is transferable to diaspora-run café ventures abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Rs 18 Lakh Debt to Rs 2 Crore Sales: A Chole Bhature Miracle
articles.excerpt: A tiny Chembur eatery was Rs 18 lakh in debt and about to close — then Abhishek Upmanyu's Instagram tip and Anushka Sharma's order for Virat Kohli turned Delhi Se into a four-outlet, Rs 2-crore-a-month brand.
articles.image_caption: Delhi Se, a 250-square-foot chole bhature outlet in Mumbai’s Chembur, now sells 3,000-plus plates a day.
articles.nri_angle: The Delhi Se turnaround shows how Indian celebrity culture can transform a small business overnight — a dynamic the diaspora watches closely, since Punjabi eateries are among the most common immigrant small businesses in the US, UK and Canada.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Harsh Goenka Savours 10-Course Vegetarian Menu at World's No. 1 Restaurant Maido
articles.excerpt: At Maido in Lima — No. 1 on the World's 50 Best Restaurants 2025 — chef Mitsuharu Tsumura created his first-ever 10-course vegetarian tasting menu, and Goenka called it memorable.
articles.image_caption: Harsh Goenka, chairman of RPG Group, shared his meal on X on September 28, 2026. He dined at Maido in Lima, Peru, ranked No. 1 on the World's 50 Best Restaurants 2025 list.
articles.nri_angle: An Indian vegetarian billionaire celebrating a plant-based tasting in Lima — a city whose Nikkei cuisine was built by the Japanese diaspora — ties two food-migration stories together.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Revant Himatsingka Quit a Rs 2 Crore US Job to Become the Food Pharmer
articles.excerpt: Speaking at NDTV Yuva 2026, the food and health activist explained why 13 years in the US convinced him that India needs better health literacy around packaged food.
articles.image_caption: Revant Himatsingka, known as Food Pharmer, left a Rs 2 crore consulting job in the US to raise awareness about packaged food.
articles.nri_angle: Himatsingka's story mirrors a growing pattern of NRIs leaving high-paying US careers to work on problems back home — here, India's packaged-food crisis.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
